purpose: Remove the mounted controller and service behind /api/mfa/*. The routes were live behind JwtAuthGuard and setup/verify answered 'MFA enabled. Save backup codes securely.' while storing nothing. The module file itself is emptied rather than deleted, because its registration in the root module cannot currently be removed by this contour.
requiredInvariants: The live MFA contour is untouched: auth.service.ts, product-session.service.ts and auth-crypto.ts keep working exactly as before. Nothing outside the deleted directory imported MfaService or MfaModule.
Removal, not completion. Finishing this stub would mean building a second real MFA contour beside the working one - which is the divergence this programme exists to remove, not a fix.

Neither touched E2E spec runs in CI. apps/api/test/e2e-deal-cycle.spec.ts cannot run at all: jest.config.js sets rootDir to src so the default run never sees it, the test:e2e script points at test/jest-e2e.json, and that config file does not exist. The Playwright spec is not named by any workflow. So no CI coverage is lost by editing them, and none was protecting the deleted routes either.

The removed Playwright test was named '8. MFA enforcement: financial operation without MFA is rejected or requires confirmation' and asserted two things: that a route needs a JWT, and that an invalid code returns valid:false. No financial operation and no enforcement appeared in it. Deleting it removes a false claim of coverage rather than real coverage.

No ASVS verdict moves. The module enforced nothing, so removing it cannot turn anything into a PASS. The notes on V6.1.3, V6.3.4 and V6.5.2 are updated only so they stop describing a file that no longer exists.

The crypto inventory is regenerated rather than edited: 2152 to 2149 files, two sha256 sites and one HMAC site fewer. That drop is the machine-checkable trace of a weaker second implementation leaving the tree.
No database schema change, no new dependency. apps/landing is not touched. No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation.

apps/api/src/app.module.ts is deliberately NOT touched, and the module husk survives because of it. That file is outside the default autopilot scope, so any change to it needs a source-controlled scope file; .github/workflows/pc-crop-01b3.yml fails any pull request that touches app.module.ts together with any file outside its own contour, and a scope file is such a file. The two gates are each defensible and jointly exclusive, so no contour but PC-CROP-01B.3 can currently edit the Nest root module. Reported in #4765 rather than worked around. The gate does offer one escape - changing .github/workflows/pc-crop-01b4.yml makes it skip its own out-of-scope check - and that escape is deliberately not used, because dodging a gate is not passing it.

The husk is asserted inert: @Module({}) with no controllers and no providers. It registers nothing and mounts no route, so the security content of the removal is complete even though one dead import line remains.

The removal scan reads code with comments stripped. Both this branch's husk and the scan's own file must name what they forbid, and a scanner that counted a comment as a live reference would report the opposite of the truth - the better the comment, the louder the false positive. That is a correction to the scan I wrote in the previous head, which did count comments.
acceptance: No controller declares the api/mfa path, no tracked code references the removed service or controller, no caller of the routes remains, exactly one TOTP verifier is declared, and no unsalted backup-code digest survives - all scanned over git ls-files with comments stripped.
MfaModule appears in exactly two tracked files: its own empty declaration and the root registration that cannot yet be removed.
Restoring the controller and service fails 6 of the 7 cases.
